episodes.209722: A surface cyclone approached the Central Coast on February 10, resulting in the first substantial rainfall in over a month for much of the Bay Area and Central Coast. A Wind Advisory was issued for all of Monterey and San Benito Counties as wind gusts up to 50 mph were expected across the region late on the 10th and into the early morning of the 11th. The orientation of the low favored rainfall for the Santa Cruz and Santa Lucia ranges, where rain totals reached 1-3 inches in the Santa Cruz Mountains, and 2-5 inches in the Santa Lucias.
episodes.211211: A strong winter storm brought significant rainfall and gusty winds to Southwestern California. Rainfall totals ranged from 0.50 to 1.50 inches across coastal and valley areas up to around 2.50 inches across the foothills and mountains. With this rainfall, numerous reports of nuisance roadway flooding was reported along with one report of flash flooding on Interstate 5. Along with the rain, gusty southerly winds developed across the higher terrain with gusts reaching up to 72 MPH.

events.narrative: Flooding was reported along the northbound side of Highway 1 just south of Pardington Lane with rocks in the roadway. Additional rockslides were reported on the highway between Lucia and the Monterey-SLO county line. The cumulative impact of all the rockslides forced the closure of Highway 1 from Pardington Lane to Ragged Point at 11 PM on February 10, reopening at 8:45 AM the next day.
California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding across all northbound lanes of Interstate 5 between Vista Del Lago Road and Smokey Bear Road. Several vehicles spun out across the flooding lanes.
